National Federation Party Leader, Professor Biman Prasad and Deputy Leader, Lenora Qereqeretabua will appear on fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan at 7pm Wednesday.

The show will focus on NFP as a partner in the coalition government, the Constitution Amendment Bill and issues surrounding it, the future of the current NFP MPs based on the party's directive, and the contentious issues currently affecting Fijians.

You can watch the show on our facebook page, YouTube channel, TikTok and X account, fijivillage at 7pm Wednesday.

You can also catch the podcast, fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan on Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

item.title: Father of man killed by soldiers in 2006 opposes immunity provisions in Constitution Bill
item.description: A father whose 19-year-old son was killed by soldiers in 2006 has spoken out against the immunity provisions, saying they have prevented him from pursuing justice for his son's death. Peni Rabaka made the submission during the public consultations on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill No. 32 of 2026 at Kshatriya Hall in Lautoka.
item.content:encoded:
A father whose 19-year-old son was killed by soldiers in 2006 has spoken out against the immunity provisions, saying they have prevented him from pursuing justice for his son's death.

Peni Rabaka made the submission during the public consultations on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill No. 32 of 2026 at Kshatriya Hall in Lautoka.

Rabaka identified himself as the father of Sakiusa Rabaka, who he says was killed by soldiers in 2006.

He told the committee that nine soldiers were involved and were released after serving only two to three weeks in prison.

Insert: Rabaka - Yellow Ribbon excuse Nov 16

Rabaka says the soldiers were released with full pay, describing their release as being justified under what he called the "yellow ribbon excuse".

He says he has been trying to pursue the case before the 2013 Constitution was introduced, and his lawyer had already filed a case.

However, Rabaka says the introduction of the 2013 Constitution saw immunity being used as the reason why the case could not proceed.

Now approaching 70, he says he is grateful to have the opportunity to present his concerns to the committee.

Rabaka told the committee that he opposes immunity in the constitution, saying he wants justice for his son.

item.title: Totoya students learn about conservation through culture and tradition
item.description: Traditional knowledge, cultural practices and environmental conservation are being brought into classroom learning in Totoya, as teachers, elders and community members work together to develop educational resources that reflect their island's heritage. The initiative brought together 25 participants, including teachers, traditional knowledge holders and community representatives, for a two-day Env
item.content:encoded:
Traditional knowledge, cultural practices and environmental conservation are being brought into classroom learning in Totoya, as teachers, elders and community members work together to develop educational resources that reflect their island's heritage.

The initiative brought together 25 participants, including teachers, traditional knowledge holders and community representatives, for a two-day Environmental Education Training of Trainers programme.

Delivered by Conservation International in partnership with local stakeholders, the programme aims to equip community members with the skills and resources to continue delivering culturally grounded environmental education in Totoya's schools and communities.

Supported by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade Manaaki Fund and the Global Environment Facility Inclusive Conservation Initiative, the programme combines traditional knowledge with modern environmental education.

It recognises the importance of passing knowledge between generations through storytelling, or talanoa, observation and practical experience .

Following the training, activities were piloted with 45 students from four villages, alongside 26 community members and teachers.

The activities included traditional weaving and creating a model of Totoya Island, allowing participants to test the learning materials and provide feedback.

Totoya District School Head Teacher Jone Draunidalo says learning outside the classroom has shown potential to improve teaching, and the school plans to apply the approach in the coming year.

He says the school intends to begin implementing what teachers have learnt in their teaching next year.

A key highlight was the involvement of the Uto ni Yalo traditional sailing canoe and its crew, which helped connect environmental education with Fiji's voyaging heritage and maritime traditions.

Students took part in hands-on activities involving traditional navigation and seafaring knowledge, learning about the relationship between culture, people and the ocean.

Uto ni Yalo crew member Josefa Kaurasi says students were introduced to the foundations of sailing and the different parts of the vessel.

The programme has also strengthened connections between educators, traditional leaders, communities and conservation practitioners, while demonstrating how local knowledge can support community-led conservation.

Conservation International Pacific Regional Project Manager Catherina Bolinga says environmental stewardship is strongest when it is rooted in local knowledge and lived experience.

She says developing learning materials that reflect Fiji's cultural and environmental contexts can help young people see their traditions and connection to nature represented in their education.

Lessons from Totoya will be used to refine the educational resources and facilitator training materials, with the potential for the approach to be adapted in other communities across Fiji.

The activities developed in Totoya will be brought together with similar work in Moala District and a national co-development workshop held in Suva in November 2025 to produce practical environmental education modules.

The resources are expected to support schools, community organisations and conservation practitioners in delivering environmental education more widely.
